lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Iodine, tin and iron are all elements, while water, ammonia and methane are compounds.
  • Ammonia can be broken down into simpler substances, so it is a compound, not an element.
  • Gram molecular mass of H2SO4 is 98 g.
  • N2 is a molecule of an element, not a compound, because it contains atoms of only one element.
  • Two moles of water contain 1.204x10^24 molecules.
  • A compound contains different kinds of atoms chemically combined together in a fixed ratio.
  • CO2 is a triatomic molecule, and hydrogen gas is a diatomic gas.
  • Air is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Choose the Correct Option

Q: i. Which one of the following group comprise of elements?

Options: (a) Mercury, water, Ammonia (b) Iodine, Tin, Iron (c) Copper, Aluminum, Methane (d) Coal, Smoke, Fog

Correct answer: Iodine, Tin, Iron

Q: ii. Which one of the following can be broken down into simpler substances?

Options: (a) Ammonia (b) Oxygen (c) Sulphur (d) Iron filling

Correct answer: Ammonia

Q: iii. The gram molecular mass of H2SO4 is:

Options: (a) 60 (b) 100 (c) 63 (d) 98

Correct answer: 98

Q: iv. Which of these molecules is not a compound?

Options: (a) N2O (b) N2 (c) NO (d) NO2

Correct answer: N2

Q: v. Which one of the following is equal to two moles of water (H2O)?

Options: (a) 1.084x10^25 molecules (b) 6.022x10^23 molecules (c) 1.204x10^24 molecules (d) 1.806x10^24 molecules

Correct answer: 1.204x10^24 molecules

Q: vi. A compound contains:

Options: (a) different kinds of atoms mixed together (b) the same kind of atoms mixed together (c) different kinds of atoms chemically combined together (d) the same kind of atoms chemically combined together

Correct answer: different kinds of atoms chemically combined together

Q: vii. Which one of the following is an example of triatomic molecule?

Options: (a) CO2 (b) O2 (c) CH4 (d) NH3

Correct answer: CO2

Q: viii. Hydrogen gas is:

Options: (a) a monoatomic gas (b) a mixture of hydrogen atoms (c) a diatomic gas with each molecule made up of two atoms (d) a diatomic atom made up of two molecules

Correct answer: a diatomic gas with each molecule made up of two atoms

Q: ix. Which one of the following compounds has both empirical and molecular formula identical?

Options: (a) Benzene (C6H6) (b) hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) (c) water (H2O) (d) glucose (C6H12O6)

Correct answer: water (H2O)

Q: x. Which one of the following is a homogeneous mixture?

Options: (a) smoke (b) air (c) fog (d) smog

Correct answer: air

mcqs.q: i. Which one of the following group comprise of elements?
mcqs.why: Iodine, tin and iron are each made of only one kind of atom, so all three are elements. The other groups contain compounds or mixtures such as water, ammonia, methane, smoke and fog.

mcqs.q: ii. Which one of the following can be broken down into simpler substances?
mcqs.why: Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen, so it can be broken down into simpler substances. Oxygen, sulphur and iron are elements and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

mcqs.q: iii. The gram molecular mass of H2SO4 is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Gram molecular mass of H2SO4 = 2(1) + 32 + 4(16). Substitution: = 2 + 32 + 64 = 98. So the gram molecular mass of H2SO4 is 98 g.

mcqs.q: iv. Which of these molecules is not a compound?
mcqs.why: N2 contains two atoms of the same element, nitrogen, so it is a molecule of an element, not a compound. N2O, NO and NO2 contain nitrogen and oxygen, two different elements, so they are compounds.

mcqs.q: v. Which one of the following is equal to two moles of water (H2O)?
mcqs.why: Formula: No. of molecules = No. of moles x Avogadro number. Substitution: = 2 x 6.022x10^23 = 1.204x10^24 molecules. So two moles of water contain 1.204x10^24 molecules.

mcqs.q: vi. A compound contains:
options: different kinds of atoms chemically combined together
different kinds of atoms mixed together
the same kind of atoms mixed together
the same kind of atoms chemically combined together
mcqs.why: A compound is formed when atoms of different elements chemically combine in a fixed ratio, for example water from hydrogen and oxygen. Mere mixing makes a mixture, and atoms of the same kind make an element molecule.

mcqs.q: vii. Which one of the following is an example of triatomic molecule?
mcqs.why: CO2 has three atoms in one molecule, one carbon and two oxygen atoms, so it is triatomic. O2 has two atoms, while CH4 has five atoms and NH3 has four atoms, so they are not triatomic.

mcqs.q: viii. Hydrogen gas is:
options: a diatomic gas with each molecule made up of two atoms
a diatomic atom made up of two molecules
mcqs.why: Each hydrogen molecule, H2, is made up of two hydrogen atoms chemically combined, so hydrogen is a diatomic gas. It is not monoatomic and it is not a mixture of separate atoms.

mcqs.q: ix. Which one of the following compounds has both empirical and molecular formula identical?
mcqs.why: For water the simplest whole number ratio of H to O is already 2:1, so its empirical formula and molecular formula are both H2O. Benzene reduces to CH, hydrogen peroxide to HO and glucose to CH2O.

mcqs.q: x. Which one of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
mcqs.why: Air has a uniform composition throughout and its components cannot be seen separately, so it is a homogeneous mixture. Smoke, fog and smog have non-uniform composition and visible particles, so they are heterogeneous.

lessons.title: Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • HF has 2 elements while Hf has 1 element; capital and small letters change the meaning of a symbol.
  • Cm is the symbol of curium because C, Cu and Cr were already used for carbon, copper and chromium.
  • Atomic number Z counts only protons; mass number A counts protons plus neutrons.
  • Mg is magnesium and Mn is manganese; K is potassium and P is phosphorus.
  • He and Ar are mono-atomic, N2 and HCl are diatomic, H2O and CO2 are tri-atomic molecules.
  • Mg2+ and Na+ are cations, O2- and Cl- are anions, and CH3 and Cl are free radicals.
  • Moles of butane in 151 g = 151 / 58 = 2.60 mol, and mass of 5 moles of ice = 5 x 18 = 90 g.
  • Average atomic mass of lithium from the given isotope data is 6.941 amu.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Short Questions

Q: i. How many elements are present in each of the following? (a) HF and Hf (b) Co and CO (c) Si and SiO2 (d) PoCl2 and POCl3

Ans: The number of elements is counted from the different element symbols in the formula. Capital and small letters matter: two letters together may be one element or two different elements.
(a) HF has 2 elements (hydrogen and fluorine), while Hf has only 1 element (hafnium).
(b) Co has only 1 element (cobalt), while CO has 2 elements (carbon and oxygen).
(c) Si has only 1 element (silicon), while SiO2 has 2 elements (silicon and oxygen).
(d) PoCl2 has 2 elements (polonium and chlorine), while POCl3 has 3 elements (phosphorus, oxygen and chlorine).

Q: ii. Cm is the chemical symbol for curium, named after the famous scientist Madam Curie. Why wasn't the symbol C, Cu or Cr used instead?

Ans: Every element has its own fixed symbol, and one symbol cannot be used for two different elements. The symbols C, Cu and Cr were already in use for other elements: C is the symbol of carbon, Cu is the symbol of copper and Cr is the symbol of chromium. So none of them could be given to curium, and a new two-letter symbol, Cm (C from Curie, with m as the second letter), was used for curium.

Q: iii. What is the atomic number of an element? How does it differ from the mass number?

Ans: The atomic number (Z) of an element is the number of protons present in the nucleus of one atom of that element. For example, the atomic number of hydrogen is 1, of carbon is 6 and of oxygen is 8.
Difference: The atomic number counts only the protons in the nucleus, while the mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons present in the nucleus (A = number of protons + number of neutrons). The atomic number is the same for all atoms of an element and identifies the element; the mass number can differ for different isotopes of the same element because the number of neutrons differs.

Q: iv. Students often mix up the following elements. Give the name for each element. (a) Mg and Mn (b) K and P (c) Na and S (d) Cu and Co

Ans: (a) Mg = Magnesium, Mn = Manganese.
(b) K = Potassium (from its Latin name Kalium), P = Phosphorus.
(c) Na = Sodium (from its Latin name Natrium), S = Sulphur.
(d) Cu = Copper (from its Latin name Cuprum), Co = Cobalt.

Q: v. a) Classify the following molecules as mono-atomic, diatomic, tri-atomic and polyatomic molecules. H2O, N2, S8, He, HCl, CO2, Ar, H2SO4, C6H12O6

Ans: Molecules are classified by the number of atoms present in one molecule.
Mono-atomic molecules (one atom): He, Ar.
Diatomic molecules (two atoms): N2, HCl.
Tri-atomic molecules (three atoms): H2O, CO2.
Polyatomic molecules (many atoms): S8 (8 atoms), H2SO4 (7 atoms), C6H12O6 (24 atoms).

Q: v. b) Classify the following as cation, anion, molecular ion, free radical and molecule. CH4+, O2-, CH3, CO+, CO2, Cl, Mg2+, CO3 2-, O2, Na+, C2H5OH-, H2O, Cl-

Ans: Cations (simple positive ions): Mg2+, Na+.
Anions (simple negative ions): O2-, Cl-.
Molecular ions (a group of atoms carrying a charge): CH4+ and CO+ (cationic molecular ions), CO3 2- and C2H5OH- (anionic molecular ions).
Free radicals (species with an unpaired electron, shown with a dot): CH3 and Cl.
Molecules (electrically neutral particles): CO2, O2, H2O.

Q: Note: Last species in Short Question v(b)

Ans: In the page scan, the printed list in Question v(b) runs off the right edge of the page after 'H2O,'. The last species is only partly visible and reads as Cl- (chloride ion); it has been classified above as an anion on that basis.

Q: vi. Calculate the number of moles of butane, C4H10 in 151 g of butane (At. masses C = 12 amu and H = 1 amu). (Ans: 2.63 moles)

Ans: Given: Mass of butane = 151 g
Atomic mass of C = 12 amu, Atomic mass of H = 1 amu
Formula: Molar mass of C4H10 = 4(Atomic mass of C) + 10(Atomic mass of H)
Substitution: Molar mass of C4H10 = 4(12) + 10(1) = 48 + 10 = 58 g/mol
Formula: No. of moles (n) = Mass (in grams) of a substance / Molar mass of the substance
Substitution: n = 151 / 58
= 2.60 moles
Answer: Number of moles of butane = 2.60 moles. (Note: the book prints the answer as 2.63 moles, but 151 / 58 = 2.60 moles.)

Q: vii. What is the mass of 5 moles of ice? (Atomic masses: H = 1 amu, O = 16 amu) (Ans: 90 g)

Ans: Given: Number of moles of ice (water) = 5 moles
Atomic mass of H = 1 amu, Atomic mass of O = 16 amu
Formula: Molar mass of H2O = 2(Atomic mass of H) + 1(Atomic mass of O)
Substitution: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol
Formula: Mass (in grams) of a substance = No. of moles (n) x Molar mass of the substance
Substitution: Mass = 5 x 18
= 90 g
Answer: The mass of 5 moles of ice = 90 g

Q: viii. Calculate the number of molecules in 6.50 mol of CH4. (Ans: 3.914x10^24 molecules)

Ans: Given: Number of moles of CH4 = 6.50 mol
Avogadro's number (NA) = 6.022 x 10^23 molecules per mole
Formula: No. of particles = No. of moles x Avogadro's number (NA)
Substitution: No. of molecules = 6.50 x 6.022 x 10^23
= 39.14 x 10^23
= 3.914 x 10^24 molecules
Answer: 6.50 mol of CH4 contains 3.914 x 10^24 molecules.

Q: ix. Calculate the average atomic mass of lithium from the following data: 6Li — Natural Abundance 7.5%, Relative Atomic Mass 6.0151 amu; 7Li — Natural Abundance 92.5%, Relative Atomic Mass 7.0160 amu. (Ans: 6.940)

Ans: Given: 6Li: abundance = 7.5%, relative atomic mass = 6.0151 amu
7Li: abundance = 92.5%, relative atomic mass = 7.0160 amu
Formula: Average atomic mass = [(Atomic mass of 1st isotope x its %age abundance) + (Atomic mass of 2nd isotope x its %age abundance)] / 100
Substitution: Average atomic mass = [(6.0151 x 7.5) + (7.0160 x 92.5)] / 100
= [45.113 + 648.98] / 100
= 694.09 / 100
= 6.9409 amu
Answer: Average atomic mass of lithium = 6.941 amu (the book prints 6.940).

Q: x. Calculate the mass of 6.68 x 10^23 molecules of PCl3. (Ans: 152.524 g)

Ans: Given: Number of molecules of PCl3 = 6.68 x 10^23
Avogadro's number (NA) = 6.023 x 10^23 molecules per mole
Atomic mass of P = 31 amu, Atomic mass of Cl = 35.5 amu
Step 1 — Molar mass:
Formula: Molar mass of PCl3 = 1(Atomic mass of P) + 3(Atomic mass of Cl)
Substitution: Molar mass of PCl3 = 31 + 3(35.5) = 31 + 106.5 = 137.5 g/mol
Step 2 — Number of moles:
Formula: No. of moles (n) = No. of particles / Avogadro's number (NA)
Substitution: n = 6.68 x 10^23 / 6.023 x 10^23 = 1.109 moles
Step 3 — Mass:
Formula: Mass (in grams) of a substance = No. of moles (n) x Molar mass of the substance
Substitution: Mass = 1.109 x 137.5
= 152.5 g
Answer: The mass of 6.68 x 10^23 molecules of PCl3 = about 152.5 g (the book prints 152.524 g).

mcqs.q: How many elements are present in HF and in Hf?
options: HF has 1 element and Hf has 2 elements
HF has 2 elements and Hf has 1 element
Both HF and Hf have 2 elements
Both HF and Hf have 1 element
mcqs.why: In HF the symbols H (hydrogen) and F (fluorine) are two different elements. In Hf the two letters together form one symbol for the single element hafnium, so letter case matters in symbols.

mcqs.q: How many elements are present in Co and in CO?
options: Co has 2 elements and CO has 1 element
Both Co and CO have 1 element
Both Co and CO have 2 elements
Co has 1 element and CO has 2 elements
mcqs.why: Co is the single symbol for cobalt, one element. CO is made of C (carbon) and O (oxygen), two different elements, so a small o and a capital O give completely different meanings.

mcqs.q: Why was the symbol Cm used for curium instead of C, Cu or Cr?
options: C, Cu and Cr were already the symbols of carbon, copper and chromium
C, Cu and Cr are symbols of the same element
Curium was discovered before carbon, copper and chromium
One symbol can be shared by two different elements
mcqs.why: Every element has its own fixed symbol and one symbol cannot be used for two elements. C was carbon, Cu was copper and Cr was chromium, so curium was given the new two-letter symbol Cm.

mcqs.q: What is the atomic number of an element?
options: The number of neutrons present in the nucleus of one atom
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus
The number of protons present in the nucleus of one atom of that element
The number of electrons in the outermost shell only
mcqs.why: Atomic number Z is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus, for example hydrogen 1, carbon 6 and oxygen 8. It is the same for all atoms of an element and identifies the element.

mcqs.q: How does the mass number differ from the atomic number?
options: Mass number is protons only, while atomic number is protons plus neutrons
Mass number and atomic number are always equal for every atom
Mass number is protons plus neutrons, while atomic number is protons only
Mass number counts only electrons, while atomic number counts protons
mcqs.why: Formula: A = number of protons + number of neutrons, while Z = number of protons only. Mass number can differ between isotopes of the same element because their neutron numbers differ.

mcqs.q: What are the names of the elements Mg and Mn?
options: Mg is magnesium and Mn is manganese
Mg is manganese and Mn is magnesium
Mg is magnesium and Mn is magnetite
Mg is manganese and Mn is molybdenum
mcqs.why: Mg and Mn are commonly mixed up. Mg stands for magnesium and Mn stands for manganese. The second letter of the symbol is different, so the two symbols represent two different elements.

mcqs.q: What are the names of the elements with symbols K and Na?
options: K is sodium and Na is potassium
K is potassium and Na is sulphur
K is phosphorus and Na is sodium
K is potassium and Na is sodium
mcqs.why: K comes from the Latin name Kalium for potassium, and Na comes from the Latin name Natrium for sodium. P is phosphorus and S is sulphur, which are different elements.

mcqs.q: Which set correctly classifies H2O, N2, He and S8 by number of atoms?
options: H2O diatomic, N2 tri-atomic, He polyatomic, S8 mono-atomic
H2O tri-atomic, N2 diatomic, He mono-atomic, S8 polyatomic
H2O mono-atomic, N2 diatomic, He tri-atomic, S8 polyatomic
H2O polyatomic, N2 mono-atomic, He diatomic, S8 tri-atomic
mcqs.why: Count the atoms in one molecule: He has 1 atom so mono-atomic, N2 has 2 atoms so diatomic, H2O has 3 atoms so tri-atomic, and S8 has 8 atoms so it is polyatomic.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a polyatomic molecule?
mcqs.why: C6H12O6 contains 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms in one molecule, so it is polyatomic. Ar is mono-atomic with 1 atom, HCl is diatomic with 2 atoms and CO2 is tri-atomic with 3 atoms.

mcqs.q: Which set correctly classifies Mg2+, O2-, CH3 and CO2?
options: Mg2+ anion, O2- cation, CH3 molecule, CO2 free radical
Mg2+ molecule, O2- free radical, CH3 cation, CO2 anion
Mg2+ cation, O2- anion, CH3 free radical, CO2 molecule
Mg2+ free radical, O2- molecule, CH3 anion, CO2 cation
mcqs.why: Mg2+ carries a positive charge so it is a cation, O2- carries a negative charge so it is an anion, CH3 has an unpaired electron so it is a free radical, and CO2 is electrically neutral so it is a molecule.

mcqs.q: Calculate the number of moles of butane, C4H10, in 151 g of butane. (Atomic masses: C = 12 amu, H = 1 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Molar mass of C4H10 = 4(12) + 10(1) = 48 + 10 = 58 g/mol. Formula: n = mass / molar mass. Substitution: n = 151 / 58 = 2.60 moles. Note: the book prints 2.63 moles, but 151 / 58 correctly gives 2.60 moles.

mcqs.q: What is the mass of 5 moles of ice? (Atomic masses: H = 1 amu, O = 16 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Formula: Mass = No. of moles x molar mass. Substitution: Mass = 5 x 18 = 90 g. So 5 moles of ice have a mass of 90 g.

mcqs.q: Calculate the number of molecules in 6.50 mol of CH4.
mcqs.why: Formula: No. of particles = No. of moles x Avogadro number. Substitution: = 6.50 x 6.022x10^23 = 39.14x10^23 = 3.914x10^24 molecules. So 6.50 mol of CH4 contains 3.914x10^24 molecules.

mcqs.q: Calculate the average atomic mass of lithium from: 6Li, abundance 7.5%, mass 6.0151 amu; 7Li, abundance 92.5%, mass 7.0160 amu.
mcqs.why: Formula: Average atomic mass = [(mass of 1st isotope x % abundance) + (mass of 2nd isotope x % abundance)] / 100. Substitution: = [(6.0151 x 7.5) + (7.0160 x 92.5)] / 100 = [45.113 + 648.98] / 100 = 6.941 amu. The book prints 6.940, but the correct value is 6.941 amu.

mcqs.q: Calculate the mass of 6.68x10^23 molecules of PCl3. (Atomic masses: P = 31 amu, Cl = 35.5 amu)
mcqs.why: Step 1: Molar mass of PCl3 = 31 + 3(35.5) = 31 + 106.5 = 137.5 g/mol. Step 2: Formula: n = particles / NA. Substitution: n = 6.68x10^23 / 6.023x10^23 = 1.109 mol. Step 3: Formula: Mass = n x molar mass = 1.109 x 137.5 = 152.5 g.

lessons.title: Detailed Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Empirical formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms, for example CH for benzene and CH2O for glucose.
  • Molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms in one molecule, and molecular formula = n x empirical formula.
  • One mole of any substance contains Avogadro number, 6.023x10^23, of particles.
  • A compound has fixed composition and cannot be separated by physical methods; a mixture can be separated physically.
  • Molecules are classified as mono-atomic, diatomic, tri-atomic and polyatomic, and as homo-atomic or hetero-atomic.
  • Molecular mass is for molecular compounds; formula mass is for ionic compounds such as NaCl and AlCl3.
  • Molecular mass of benzene C6H6 is 78 amu and formula mass of Fe2O3 is 160 amu.
  • In a neutral atom, number of protons = number of electrons = atomic number, and neutrons = A - Z.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Long Questions

Q: (i) State and explain with examples: (a) The empirical formula of a compound. (b) The molecular formula of a compound.

Ans: (a) Empirical formula: The empirical formula of a chemical compound is the simplest formula which shows the smallest whole number ratio of the atoms of the different elements present in the compound. It may not be the actual formula of the compound. For example, the actual (molecular) formula of benzene is C6H6; the ratio of carbon to hydrogen atoms is 6:6, i.e. the simplest ratio 1:1, so its empirical formula is CH. Glucose has the molecular formula C6H12O6; the simplest ratio of C:H:O is 1:2:1, so its empirical formula is CH2O.
(b) Molecular formula: The molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of different elements present in one molecule of that compound. For example, the molecular formula of glucose is C6H12O6 (one molecule contains 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen and 6 oxygen atoms) and the molecular formula of benzene is C6H6. The molecular formula is obtained from the empirical formula by the relation: Molecular formula = n x (Empirical formula), where n = 1, 2, 3, 4, ... For benzene, n = 6, so its molecular formula = 6(CH) = C6H6. A molecular formula may be the same as, or a whole-number multiple of, the empirical formula.

Q: (ii) What do you understand by the terms mole and Avogadro's number? Explain with suitable examples.

Ans: Mole: Chemists use a counting unit called mole to measure the amount of a substance. A mole is defined as the amount (mass) of a substance which contains Avogadro's number (6.023 x 10^23) particles (atoms, molecules or ions). It is represented as 'mol'. The mass of a substance may be atomic mass, molecular mass or formula mass; when these masses are expressed in grams they are called molar masses, so a mole can be quantitatively defined as the atomic mass, molecular mass or formula mass of a substance expressed in grams. Examples: 12 g of carbon = 1 mole of carbon; 18 g of water = 1 mole of water; 98 g of H2SO4 = 1 mole of sulphuric acid; 58.5 g of NaCl = 1 mole of sodium chloride.
Avogadro's number: Avogadro's number is defined as the number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in one mole of any substance, and it is numerically equal to 6.023 x 10^23. It is represented by the symbol NA and was determined by the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro. Examples: 1.0 g of hydrogen = 1 mole = 6.023 x 10^23 atoms of hydrogen; 12 g of carbon = 1 mole = 6.023 x 10^23 atoms of carbon; 18 g of water = 1 mole = 6.023 x 10^23 molecules of water; 58.5 g of NaCl = 1 mole = 6.023 x 10^23 formula units of NaCl.

Q: (iii) (a) Compare and contrast a mixture and a compound. Give examples of each of them.

Ans: A compound is formed by the chemical combination of atoms of different elements, while a mixture is formed by the physical combination (mixing up) of two or more substances.
In a compound, the constituents lose their original properties; in a mixture, the constituents retain their properties.
A compound always has a fixed composition by mass; a mixture does not have a fixed composition by mass.
The components of a compound cannot be separated by physical methods; the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
Every compound is represented by its chemical formula; a mixture consists of two or more components and does not have any chemical formula.
A compound has a homogeneous composition; a mixture may be homogeneous or heterogeneous in composition.
A compound has a sharp and fixed melting point; a mixture does not have a sharp and fixed melting point.
Examples: Compound — water (H2O), common salt (NaCl). Mixture — air, and iron filings mixed with sulphur (the iron can be separated from the sulphur with a magnet, and both retain their properties; on strong heating they form the compound iron sulphide, FeS, which cannot be separated by a magnet).

Q: (iii) (b) How will you classify molecules? Support your answer with at least two examples of each.

Ans: Molecules are classified in two ways.
(1) By the number of atoms present in the molecule: (i) Mono-atomic molecules, made up of only one atom, e.g. helium (He) and argon (Ar) — the inert gases. (ii) Di-atomic molecules, consisting of two atoms, e.g. hydrogen (H2) and oxygen (O2) (also hydrochloric acid, HCl). (iii) Tri-atomic molecules, consisting of three atoms, e.g. water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) (also ozone, O3). (iv) Poly-atomic molecules, made up of many atoms, e.g. sulphuric acid (H2SO4) and sugar (C12H22O11) (also the sulphur molecule, S8).
(2) By the nature of the atoms present in the molecule: (i) Homo-atomic molecules, which consist of atoms of the same element, e.g. oxygen (O2) and hydrogen (H2) (also chlorine, Cl2, and sulphur, S8). (ii) Hetero-atomic molecules, which consist of atoms of different elements, e.g. carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O) (also hydrochloric acid, HCl).

Q: (iv) (a) What is the molecular mass of a compound? How will you differentiate it from formula mass?

Ans: Molecular mass: Molecular mass is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms present in one molecule of a substance. It is calculated by adding the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in one molecule. For example, the molecular mass of ethane (C2H6) = 2(atomic mass of C) + 6(atomic mass of H) = 2(12) + 6(1) = 24 + 6 = 30 a.m.u.
Difference from formula mass: Molecular mass is used for molecular (covalent) compounds, which exist as separate molecules, and it is the mass of one molecule. Formula mass is used for ionic compounds, which do not exist as separate molecules but as formula units in a crystal lattice; it is the sum of the atomic masses of the ions (atoms) present in one formula unit of the ionic compound. For example, the formula mass of NaCl = 1(atomic mass of Na) + 1(atomic mass of Cl) = 23 a.m.u. + 35.5 a.m.u. = 58.5 a.m.u. Both are calculated in the same manner; only the name differs with the type of compound.

Q: (iv) (b) (i) Calculate the molecular mass or formula mass, as the case may be, of Benzene, C6H6, in amu.

Ans: Given: Atomic mass of C = 12 amu, Atomic mass of H = 1 amu
Formula: Molecular mass = Sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule
Substitution: Molecular mass of C6H6 = 6(12) + 6(1)
= 72 + 6
= 78 amu
Answer: Molecular mass of benzene = 78 amu

Q: (iv) (b) (ii) Calculate the molecular mass or formula mass, as the case may be, of Ethane gas, C2H6, in amu.

Ans: Given: Atomic mass of C = 12 amu, Atomic mass of H = 1 amu
Formula: Molecular mass = Sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule
Substitution: Molecular mass of C2H6 = 2(12) + 6(1)
= 24 + 6
= 30 amu
Answer: Molecular mass of ethane = 30 amu

Q: (iv) (b) (iii) Calculate the molecular mass or formula mass, as the case may be, of Aluminum chloride, AlCl3, in amu.

Ans: Given: Atomic mass of Al = 27 amu, Atomic mass of Cl = 35.5 amu
AlCl3 is an ionic compound, so its formula mass is calculated.
Formula: Formula mass = Sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the formula unit
Substitution: Formula mass of AlCl3 = 1(27) + 3(35.5)
= 27 + 106.5
= 133.5 amu
Answer: Formula mass of aluminum chloride = 133.5 amu

Q: (iv) (b) (iv) Calculate the molecular mass or formula mass, as the case may be, of Iron oxide, Fe2O3, in amu.

Ans: Given: Atomic mass of Fe = 56 amu, Atomic mass of O = 16 amu
Fe2O3 is an ionic compound, so its formula mass is calculated.
Formula: Formula mass = Sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the formula unit
Substitution: Formula mass of Fe2O3 = 2(56) + 3(16)
= 112 + 48
= 160 amu
Answer: Formula mass of iron oxide = 160 amu

Q: (v) (a) Find out the number of protons, electrons and neutrons in the following elements: 23Na (Z=11), 107Ag (Z=47), 56Fe (Z=26), 207Pb (Z=82), 40Ar (Z=18), 238U (Z=92).

Ans: Formula: Number of protons = Atomic number (Z)
Number of electrons = Number of protons (in a neutral atom)
Number of neutrons = Mass number (A) − Atomic number (Z)
23Na (Z = 11, A = 23): Protons = 11, Electrons = 11, Neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12
107Ag (Z = 47, A = 107): Protons = 47, Electrons = 47, Neutrons = 107 − 47 = 60
56Fe (Z = 26, A = 56): Protons = 26, Electrons = 26, Neutrons = 56 − 26 = 30
207Pb (Z = 82, A = 207): Protons = 82, Electrons = 82, Neutrons = 207 − 82 = 125
40Ar (Z = 18, A = 40): Protons = 18, Electrons = 18, Neutrons = 40 − 18 = 22
238U (Z = 92, A = 238): Protons = 92, Electrons = 92, Neutrons = 238 − 92 = 146

Q: (v) (b) Complete the following table: (a) Symbol K; (b) Atomic No. 8; (c) Number of Protons 15, Number of electrons 15; (d) Atomic No. 20; (e) Symbol Cl. Columns: Symbol, Atomic No., Number of Protons, Number of electrons.

Ans: In a neutral atom, Atomic No. = Number of Protons = Number of electrons, and the atomic number identifies the element.
a. Symbol = K (potassium), Atomic No. = 19, Number of Protons = 19, Number of electrons = 19
b. Symbol = O (oxygen), Atomic No. = 8, Number of Protons = 8, Number of electrons = 8
c. Symbol = P (phosphorus), Atomic No. = 15, Number of Protons = 15, Number of electrons = 15
d. Symbol = Ca (calcium), Atomic No. = 20, Number of Protons = 20, Number of electrons = 20
e. Symbol = Cl (chlorine), Atomic No. = 17, Number of Protons = 17, Number of electrons = 17

mcqs.q: What is the empirical formula of benzene, C6H6?
mcqs.why: The ratio of carbon to hydrogen atoms in C6H6 is 6:6, which reduces to the simplest whole number ratio 1:1. So the empirical formula of benzene is CH, while C6H6 is its molecular formula.

mcqs.q: What is a mole of a substance?
options: The amount of a substance which contains 100 particles
One gram of any substance, whatever its particles
The number of atoms present in one molecule of a substance
The amount of a substance which contains Avogadro number (6.023x10^23) of particles
mcqs.why: A mole is the counting unit for amount of substance and always contains 6.023x10^23 particles, atoms, molecules or ions. Examples are 12 g of carbon, 18 g of water and 58.5 g of NaCl, each equal to one mole.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly compares a compound and a mixture?
options: A compound has a fixed composition by mass, while a mixture does not have a fixed composition
A mixture has a fixed composition by mass, while a compound does not
Both a compound and a mixture always have a sharp fixed melting point
A compound can be separated by physical methods, while a mixture cannot
mcqs.why: In a compound the elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio and lose their original properties, and separation needs chemical methods. In a mixture the components keep their properties, have no fixed composition and can be separated physically.

mcqs.q: Which pair is an example of homo-atomic and hetero-atomic molecules respectively?
options: CO2 is homo-atomic and O2 is hetero-atomic
O2 and CO2 are both homo-atomic
O2 is homo-atomic and CO2 is hetero-atomic
O2 and CO2 are both hetero-atomic
mcqs.why: O2 is made of atoms of the same element, oxygen only, so it is homo-atomic. CO2 is made of carbon and oxygen, different elements, so it is hetero-atomic. Classification by kind of atoms gives these two types.

mcqs.q: How does formula mass differ from molecular mass?
options: Formula mass is always greater than molecular mass for the same substance
Molecular mass is used for ionic compounds, while formula mass is used for gases only
Formula mass is used for ionic compounds that exist as formula units, while molecular mass is the mass of one molecule of a molecular compound
Formula mass is calculated in kilograms, while molecular mass is calculated in grams
mcqs.why: Molecular compounds exist as separate molecules, so we speak of molecular mass. Ionic compounds such as NaCl do not exist as separate molecules but as formula units in a lattice, so the sum of atomic masses in one formula unit is called formula mass.

mcqs.q: Calculate the molecular mass of benzene, C6H6, in amu. (Atomic masses: C = 12 amu, H = 1 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Molecular mass = sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the molecule. Substitution: Molecular mass of C6H6 = 6(12) + 6(1) = 72 + 6 = 78 amu. So the molecular mass of benzene is 78 amu.

mcqs.q: Calculate the formula mass of aluminium chloride, AlCl3, in amu. (Atomic masses: Al = 27 amu, Cl = 35.5 amu)
mcqs.why: AlCl3 is an ionic compound, so formula mass is calculated. Formula: Formula mass = sum of atomic masses in one formula unit. Substitution: = 1(27) + 3(35.5) = 27 + 106.5 = 133.5 amu.

mcqs.q: Calculate the formula mass of iron oxide, Fe2O3, in amu. (Atomic masses: Fe = 56 amu, O = 16 amu)
mcqs.why: Fe2O3 is an ionic compound, so formula mass is calculated. Formula: Formula mass = sum of atomic masses in one formula unit. Substitution: = 2(56) + 3(16) = 112 + 48 = 160 amu.

mcqs.q: How many protons, electrons and neutrons are present in 56Fe, where Z = 26?
mcqs.why: Formula: Protons = Z = 26. In a neutral atom electrons = protons = 26. Formula: Neutrons = A - Z. Substitution: Neutrons = 56 - 26 = 30. So iron-56 has 26 protons, 26 electrons and 30 neutrons.

mcqs.q: An element has atomic number 20. What is its symbol and how many protons and electrons does its neutral atom have?
options: Potassium, K, with 19 protons and 19 electrons
Calcium, Ca, with 20 protons and 18 electrons
Calcium, Ca, with 20 protons and 20 electrons
Chlorine, Cl, with 17 protons and 17 electrons
mcqs.why: In a neutral atom, atomic number = number of protons = number of electrons, and the atomic number identifies the element. Atomic number 20 is calcium, Ca, so it has 20 protons and 20 electrons.

lessons.title: Test Yourself and Practice Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Analytical chemistry deals with qualitative and quantitative analysis, such as the amount of an impurity in drinking water.
  • Developing a medicine is industrial chemistry, because a medicine is prepared as an industrial product.
  • Sand in water and oil in water are heterogeneous mixtures; baking soda in water and ink in water are homogeneous.
  • For lithium with 3 protons and 4 neutrons, Z = 3, A = 7 and electrons = 3.
  • Hydrogen (protium) is the element whose ordinary atom has no neutron.
  • Average atomic mass of gallium is 69.723 amu and of neon is 20.187 amu from the given data.
  • Formula mass of KCl is 74.5 amu and of Na2CO3 is 106 amu.
  • 90 g of water is 5 moles, and 5 moles of glucose contain 3.0115x10^24 molecules.

Solved Exercises

Test Yourself (Branches of Chemistry)

Q: (a) A chemist mostly uses which branch of chemistry to determine the amount of an impurity in drinking water?

Ans: Analytical chemistry. Analytical chemistry deals with the qualitative and quantitative analysis of matter, so finding how much (the amount) of an impurity is present in a sample of drinking water is quantitative analysis, which belongs to analytical chemistry.

Q: (b) A chemist in which branch of chemistry determines the composition of a substance and determines their masses?

Ans: Analytical chemistry. Determining what a substance is made of (its composition) and how much of each component is present (their masses) is the analysis of matter, which is the work of analytical chemistry.

Q: (c) A chemist develops a medicine to help patients with thyroid problems. In which branch of chemistry is this chemist working?

Ans: Industrial chemistry. Industrial chemistry deals with the techniques and chemical processes used for the preparation of different industrial products. A medicine is prepared/manufactured as an industrial product (like cement, glass and fertilizers), so developing a medicine is the work of industrial chemistry.

Activity 1.1

Q: Make a list of ten elements other than the above one (Table 1.2), with their names and symbols. Also write down uses of five elements in daily life.

Ans: Ten more elements: 1. Helium — He, 2. Lithium — Li, 3. Neon — Ne, 4. Silicon — Si, 5. Phosphorus — P, 6. Chlorine — Cl, 7. Argon — Ar, 8. Zinc — Zn, 9. Iodine — I, 10. Chromium — Cr.
Uses of five elements in daily life: (1) Oxygen — used by living things for breathing (respiration) and for burning. (2) Carbon — used as fuel (coal), and as graphite in pencils. (3) Aluminium — used for cooking utensils, cans and window frames because it is light and does not rust easily. (4) Copper — used for electric wires because it is a very good conductor of electricity. (5) Chlorine — used to kill germs in drinking water and swimming pools.

Practice Problem 1.1

Q: Making mixtures: Make mixtures of sand, baking soda, ink and oil in water. Classify these as heterogeneous or homogeneous. Give reasons for your choice.

Ans: (1) Sand in water — Heterogeneous mixture. Sand does not dissolve in water; its particles remain separate, can be seen, and settle down on standing, so the composition is not uniform throughout.
(2) Baking soda in water — Homogeneous mixture. Baking soda dissolves completely in water and forms a uniform solution; no separate particles can be seen.
(3) Ink in water — Homogeneous mixture. Ink spreads and mixes uniformly in water, giving a solution of the same colour and composition throughout.
(4) Oil in water — Heterogeneous mixture. Oil does not dissolve or mix with water; it floats as a separate layer on the water, so the composition is not uniform.

Test Yourself (Atomic Number and Mass Number)

Q: 1. An atom of Lithium has three protons and four neutrons in its nucleus. (a) What is its atomic number and atomic mass? (b) How many electrons does it have?

Ans: Given: Number of protons = 3
Number of neutrons = 4
Formula: Atomic number (Z) = Number of protons
Mass number (A) = Number of protons + Number of neutrons
Substitution: Z = 3
A = 3 + 4 = 7
(a) Atomic number of lithium = 3 and its atomic mass (mass number) = 7.
(b) An atom is electrically neutral, so the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
Number of electrons = Number of protons = 3
Answer: (a) Atomic number = 3, atomic mass = 7 (b) Electrons = 3

Q: 2. The atomic number of Iron is 26 and atomic mass is 56. (a) How many protons and electrons does an iron atom have? (b) How many neutrons does an Iron atom have?

Ans: Given: Atomic number (Z) of iron = 26
Atomic mass (mass number, A) = 56
Formula: Number of protons = Atomic number (Z)
Number of electrons = Number of protons (in a neutral atom)
Number of neutrons = Mass number (A) − Atomic number (Z)
Substitution: Number of protons = 26
Number of electrons = 26
Number of neutrons = 56 − 26 = 30
Answer: (a) Protons = 26 and electrons = 26 (b) Neutrons = 30

Q: 3. Do you know any element having no neutron in its atom?

Ans: Yes — hydrogen. The common atom of hydrogen (protium) has only one proton and one electron in its atom and no neutron in its nucleus. It is the only element whose ordinary atom has no neutron.

Practice Problem 1.2

Q: Naturally occurring gallium consists of 60.108% Ga-69, with a mass of 68.9256 amu, and 39.892% Ga-71, with a mass of 70.9247 amu. Calculate the average atomic mass of gallium.

Ans: Given: Ga-69: abundance = 60.108%, atomic mass = 68.9256 amu
Ga-71: abundance = 39.892%, atomic mass = 70.9247 amu
Formula: Average atomic mass = [(Atomic mass of 1st isotope x its %age abundance) + (Atomic mass of 2nd isotope x its %age abundance)] / 100
Substitution: Average atomic mass = [(68.9256 x 60.108) + (70.9247 x 39.892)] / 100
= [4142.98 + 2829.33] / 100
= 6972.31 / 100
= 69.723 amu
Answer: Average atomic mass of gallium = 69.723 amu

Q: Calculate the atomic mass of neon from the given data: 20Ne = 90.51%, 21Ne = 0.27%, 22Ne = 9.22%.

Ans: Given: 20Ne: abundance = 90.51%
21Ne: abundance = 0.27%
22Ne: abundance = 9.22%
The book gives only the percentage abundances, so the mass of each isotope is taken as its mass number (20, 21 and 22 amu), as done for chlorine in the unit text.
Formula: Average atomic mass = [(Mass of 1st isotope x its %age abundance) + (Mass of 2nd isotope x its %age abundance) + (Mass of 3rd isotope x its %age abundance)] / 100
Substitution: Average atomic mass = [(20 x 90.51) + (21 x 0.27) + (22 x 9.22)] / 100
= [1810.2 + 5.67 + 202.84] / 100
= 2018.71 / 100
= 20.187 amu
Answer: Atomic mass of neon = 20.187 amu (about 20.19 amu)

Practice Problem 1.3

Q: How many atoms of each element are present in one formula unit of each of the following compounds? (a) Hg2Cl2 (b) NH4H2PO4 (c) MgCl2 (d) NH4OH

Ans: The subscript after a symbol shows the number of atoms of that element in one formula unit; no subscript means one atom.
(a) Hg2Cl2: Mercury (Hg) = 2 atoms, Chlorine (Cl) = 2 atoms.
(b) NH4H2PO4: Nitrogen (N) = 1 atom, Hydrogen (H) = 4 + 2 = 6 atoms, Phosphorus (P) = 1 atom, Oxygen (O) = 4 atoms.
(c) MgCl2: Magnesium (Mg) = 1 atom, Chlorine (Cl) = 2 atoms.
(d) NH4OH: Nitrogen (N) = 1 atom, Hydrogen (H) = 4 + 1 = 5 atoms, Oxygen (O) = 1 atom.

Practice Problem 1.4

Q: Calculate the formula mass of (a) KCl and (b) Na2CO3.

Ans: (a) KCl
Given: Atomic mass of K = 39 amu, Atomic mass of Cl = 35.5 amu
Formula: Formula mass = Sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the formula unit
Substitution: Formula mass of KCl = 1(39) + 1(35.5)
= 39 + 35.5
= 74.5 amu
Answer: Formula mass of KCl = 74.5 amu
(b) Na2CO3
Given: Atomic mass of Na = 23 amu, Atomic mass of C = 12 amu, Atomic mass of O = 16 amu
Formula: Formula mass = Sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the formula unit
Substitution: Formula mass of Na2CO3 = 2(23) + 1(12) + 3(16)
= 46 + 12 + 48
= 106 amu
Answer: Formula mass of Na2CO3 = 106 amu

Practice Problem 1.5

Q: How many moles are there in 90 g of water (H2O)?

Ans: Given: Mass of water = 90 g
Atomic mass of H = 1 amu, Atomic mass of O = 16 amu
Formula: Molar mass of H2O = 2(Atomic mass of H) + 1(Atomic mass of O)
Substitution: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol
Formula: No. of moles (n) = Mass (in grams) of a substance / Molar mass of the substance
Substitution: n = 90 / 18
= 5 moles
Answer: There are 5 moles in 90 g of water.

Practice Problem 1.5 (second, p34)

Q: a. How many moles of CO2 are there in 3.01 x 10^23 molecules of CO2?

Ans: Given: Number of molecules of CO2 = 3.01 x 10^23
Avogadro's number (NA) = 6.023 x 10^23 particles per mole
Formula: No. of moles (n) = No. of particles / Avogadro's number (NA)
Substitution: n = 3.01 x 10^23 / 6.023 x 10^23
= 0.5 mole
Answer: There are 0.5 moles of CO2 in 3.01 x 10^23 molecules of CO2.

Q: b. Calculate the number of molecules present in 5 moles of glucose C6H12O6.

Ans: Given: Number of moles of glucose = 5 moles
Avogadro's number (NA) = 6.023 x 10^23 molecules per mole
Formula: No. of particles = No. of moles x Avogadro's number (NA)
Substitution: No. of molecules = 5 x 6.023 x 10^23
= 30.115 x 10^23
= 3.0115 x 10^24 molecules
Answer: 5 moles of glucose contain 3.0115 x 10^24 molecules (about 3.01 x 10^24 molecules).

mcqs.q: A chemist determines the amount of an impurity in drinking water. Which branch of chemistry is mostly used?
mcqs.why: Finding how much of an impurity is present is quantitative analysis of matter. Analytical chemistry deals with the qualitative and quantitative analysis of matter, so this work belongs to analytical chemistry.

mcqs.q: A chemist develops a medicine to help patients with thyroid problems. In which branch of chemistry is this chemist working?
mcqs.why: Industrial chemistry deals with the techniques and processes used for the preparation of industrial products. A medicine is manufactured as an industrial product like cement, glass and fertilizers, so developing it is industrial chemistry.

mcqs.q: Which element and use pair is correct from daily life examples?
options: Copper is used for electric wires because it is a very good conductor of electricity
Copper is used to kill germs in swimming pools
Chlorine is used for electric wires because it conducts electricity
Aluminium is used as graphite in pencils
mcqs.why: Copper is a very good conductor of electricity, so it is used for electric wires. Chlorine is used to kill germs in water, aluminium is used for utensils and cans, and carbon as graphite is used in pencils.

mcqs.q: How are sand in water and baking soda in water classified?
options: Sand in water is homogeneous and baking soda in water is heterogeneous
Sand in water is heterogeneous and baking soda in water is homogeneous
mcqs.why: Sand does not dissolve in water, its particles can be seen and settle on standing, so it is heterogeneous. Baking soda dissolves completely and forms a uniform solution, so it is a homogeneous mixture.

mcqs.q: An atom of lithium has three protons and four neutrons in its nucleus. What are its atomic number and mass number?
mcqs.why: Formula: Atomic number Z = number of protons = 3. Formula: Mass number A = protons + neutrons. Substitution: A = 3 + 4 = 7. So lithium has atomic number 3 and mass number 7, and 3 electrons in a neutral atom.

mcqs.q: The atomic number of iron is 26 and its atomic mass is 56. How many neutrons does an iron atom have?
mcqs.why: Formula: Number of neutrons = mass number A - atomic number Z. Substitution: Neutrons = 56 - 26 = 30. The iron atom also has 26 protons and, being neutral, 26 electrons.

mcqs.q: Which element has no neutron in its ordinary atom?
mcqs.why: The common atom of hydrogen, protium, has only one proton and one electron and no neutron in its nucleus. It is the only element whose ordinary atom has no neutron.

mcqs.q: Naturally occurring gallium consists of 60.108% Ga-69 (mass 68.9256 amu) and 39.892% Ga-71 (mass 70.9247 amu). Calculate its average atomic mass.
mcqs.why: Formula: Average atomic mass = [(mass of 1st isotope x % abundance) + (mass of 2nd isotope x % abundance)] / 100. Substitution: = [(68.9256 x 60.108) + (70.9247 x 39.892)] / 100 = [4142.98 + 2829.33] / 100 = 69.723 amu.

mcqs.q: Calculate the atomic mass of neon from: 20Ne = 90.51%, 21Ne = 0.27%, 22Ne = 9.22%, taking each isotope mass as its mass number.
How many atoms of each element are present in one formula unit of NH4H2PO4?
mcqs.why: The subscript after a symbol shows the number of atoms of that element. Hydrogen appears twice: 4 from NH4 and 2 from H2, so H = 4 + 2 = 6. Nitrogen is 1, phosphorus is 1 and oxygen is 4.

mcqs.q: Calculate the formula mass of KCl. (Atomic masses: K = 39 amu, Cl = 35.5 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Formula mass = sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the formula unit. Substitution: Formula mass of KCl = 1(39) + 1(35.5) = 39 + 35.5 = 74.5 amu.

mcqs.q: Calculate the formula mass of Na2CO3. (Atomic masses: Na = 23 amu, C = 12 amu, O = 16 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Formula mass = sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the formula unit. Substitution: Formula mass of Na2CO3 = 2(23) + 1(12) + 3(16) = 46 + 12 + 48 = 106 amu.

mcqs.q: How many moles are there in 90 g of water, H2O? (Atomic masses: H = 1 amu, O = 16 amu)
mcqs.why: Formula: Molar mass of H2O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Formula: n = mass / molar mass. Substitution: n = 90 / 18 = 5 moles. So 90 g of water contains 5 moles.

mcqs.q: How many moles of CO2 are there in 3.01x10^23 molecules of CO2?
mcqs.why: Formula: No. of moles n = No. of particles / Avogadro number NA. Substitution: n = 3.01x10^23 / 6.023x10^23 = 0.5 mole. So 3.01x10^23 molecules of CO2 make half a mole.

mcqs.q: Calculate the number of molecules present in 5 moles of glucose, C6H12O6.
mcqs.why: Formula: No. of particles = No. of moles x Avogadro number NA. Substitution: No. of molecules = 5 x 6.023x10^23 = 30.115x10^23 = 3.0115x10^24 molecules, about 3.01x10^24 molecules.

lessons.title: Project Work
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In an atom model, the protons and neutrons are shown together in the central nucleus and the electrons in shells around it.
  • Sodium (23Na, Z = 11) has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 12 neutrons (23 - 11).
  • Carbon (12C, Z = 6) has 6 protons, 6 electrons and 6 neutrons (12 - 6).
  • Oxygen (16O, Z = 8) has 8 protons, 8 electrons and 8 neutrons (16 - 8).
  • Number of neutrons = mass number (A) - atomic number (Z); number of electrons = number of protons in a neutral atom.

Solved Exercises

Project Work

Q: Prepare the model of sodium, carbon and oxygen, showing number of protons, electrons and neutrons and present in the class.

Ans: Make one model (balls of different colours for protons, neutrons and electrons) for each atom, using: Number of protons = Atomic number (Z); Number of electrons = Number of protons; Number of neutrons = Mass number (A) − Atomic number (Z).
Sodium, 23Na (Z = 11): Protons = 11, Electrons = 11, Neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12.
Carbon, 12C (Z = 6): Protons = 6, Electrons = 6, Neutrons = 12 − 6 = 6.
Oxygen, 16O (Z = 8): Protons = 8, Electrons = 8, Neutrons = 16 − 8 = 8.
In each model, show the protons and neutrons together in the central nucleus and the electrons in shells around the nucleus, and label the numbers of protons, electrons and neutrons when presenting in the class.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Maximum number of electrons in the third energy level (M shell) is 18, from 2n2 with n = 3.
  • Mass of an atom is mostly due to its nucleus, which contains protons and neutrons.
  • Neutrons have no charge, so they would not deflect in a scattering experiment.
  • An electron in its ground state does not radiate energy.
  • Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons and mass numbers.
  • An electron is the lightest among an alpha particle, a hydrogen atom, a proton and an electron.
  • The nucleus contains nearly all the mass of the atom but very little of its volume.
  • The L-shell has s and p sub-shells.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Choose the Correct Option

Q: i. The maximum number of electrons in third energy level is:

Options: (a) 10 (b) 18 (c) 32 (d) 64

Correct answer: 18

Q: ii. Mass of an atom is mostly due to its

Options: (a) nucleus (b) neutrons (c) electrons (d) protons

Correct answer: nucleus

Q: iii. If Rutherford had used neutrons instead of alpha particles in his scattering experiment, the neutrons would

Options: (a) not deflect because they have no charge (b) have deflected more often (c) have been attracted to the nucleus easily (d) have given the same results

Correct answer: not deflect because they have no charge

Q: iv. Electron in its ground state does not

Options: (a) spin (b) revolve (c) radiate energy (d) reside in orbit

Correct answer: radiate energy

Q: v. Which statement about 17/8 X and 18/8 Y is false?

Options: (a) they are isotopes (b) they are the same elements (c) they have the same number of electrons (d) they have the same number of neutrons

Correct answer: they have the same number of neutrons

Q: vi. The neutron particle

Options: (a) has a mass equal to that of an electron (b) has a mass approximately equal to that of a proton (c) has charge equal to but opposite to that of an electron (d) has a positive charge

Correct answer: has a mass approximately equal to that of a proton

Q: vii. Isotopes of the same element have

Options: (a) the same number of protons (b) the same number of neutrons (c) different number of electrons (d) the same mass number

Correct answer: the same number of protons

Q: viii. Which one is the lightest?

Options: (a) an alpha particle (b) a hydrogen atom (c) an electron (d) a proton

Correct answer: an electron

Q: ix. The nucleus of an atom has all of the following characteristics except that it

Options: (a) is positively charged (b) is very dense (c) contains nearly all of the atom's mass (d) contains nearly all of the atom's volume

Correct answer: contains nearly all of the atom's volume

Q: x. L-shell has sub-shell(s)

Options: (a) s (b) s and p (c) s, p and d (d) s, p, d and f

Correct answer: s and p

mcqs.q: i. The maximum number of electrons in third energy level is:
mcqs.why: Formula: Maximum electrons in a shell = 2n2. For the third energy level n = 3. Substitution: 2(3)2 = 2 x 9 = 18. So the third energy level can hold at most 18 electrons.

mcqs.q: ii. Mass of an atom is mostly due to its
mcqs.why: Protons and neutrons are both present in the nucleus and each is about 1837 or more times heavier than an electron. The mass of electrons is negligible, so the mass of an atom is mostly due to its nucleus as a whole.

mcqs.q: iii. If Rutherford had used neutrons instead of alpha particles in his scattering experiment, the neutrons would
options: not deflect because they have no charge
have been attracted to the nucleus easily
mcqs.why: Deflection in the gold foil experiment happened because positively charged alpha particles were repelled by the positive nucleus. Neutrons carry no charge, so there would be no such repulsion and they would not deflect.

mcqs.q: iv. Electron in its ground state does not
mcqs.why: According to Bohr, as long as an electron revolves in a fixed orbit of fixed energy in its ground state, it does not gain or lose, that is radiate, energy. It radiates energy only when it jumps to a lower energy orbit.

mcqs.q: v. Which statement about 17/8 X and 18/8 Y is false?
options: they have the same number of neutrons
they have the same number of electrons
mcqs.why: Both have atomic number 8, so they are the same element and isotopes with the same electrons. Neutrons: for X, 17 - 8 = 9; for Y, 18 - 8 = 10. Their neutron numbers differ, so the statement that they have the same number of neutrons is false.

mcqs.q: vi. The neutron particle
options: has a mass approximately equal to that of a proton
has a mass equal to that of an electron
has charge equal to but opposite to that of an electron
mcqs.why: A neutron has mass 1.0086654 amu, close to a proton at 1.0072766 amu, and far greater than an electron at 0.000548597 amu. A neutron carries no charge at all, so it is neutral.

mcqs.q: vii. Isotopes of the same element have
mcqs.why: Isotopes have the same atomic number, which means the same number of protons, and in neutral atoms the same number of electrons. They differ in number of neutrons, so their mass numbers are different.

mcqs.q: viii. Which one is the lightest?
mcqs.why: An electron has a mass of only 0.000548597 amu, while a proton is about 1837 times heavier, a hydrogen atom contains a proton, and an alpha particle is heavier still. So the electron is the lightest.

mcqs.q: ix. The nucleus of an atom has all of the following characteristics except that it
options: contains nearly all of the atom's volume
contains nearly all of the atom's mass
mcqs.why: The nucleus is positively charged, very dense and contains nearly all the mass of the atom, but it is very small compared with the atom. Most of the volume of the atom is empty space, so the nucleus does not contain nearly all the volume.

mcqs.q: x. L-shell has sub-shell(s)
mcqs.why: The L-shell is the second shell, n = 2, and it is divided into two sub-shells, 2s and 2p. The d sub-shell starts from the M shell and the f sub-shell from the N shell.

lessons.title: Short Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Aluminium 27/13 Al has 13 protons, 14 neutrons, 13 electrons and configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1.
  • Shell energy increases with distance from the nucleus, so L shell electrons have higher energy than K shell electrons.
  • An atom is neutral because the number of protons equals the number of electrons and their charges cancel.
  • Isotopes have the same chemical properties because they have the same electrons, but different physical properties because their masses differ.
  • Maximum electrons in shells K, L, M, N are 2, 8, 18, 32 by the formula 2n2.
  • Carbon-14 has 6 protons, 8 neutrons and 6 electrons.
  • Potassium with arrangement 2,8,8,1 has proton number 19, the total of its electrons.
  • In the Bohr model made in Activity 2.1, each electron stays on a fixed circle of fixed energy and cannot stay between orbits.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Short Questions

Q: i. Aluminum is represented as 27/13 Al. Draw the structures of Aluminum. Write its electronic configuration.

Ans: Atomic number (Z) = 13, so a neutral aluminium atom has 13 protons and 13 electrons. Mass number (A) = 27, so neutrons = A − Z = 27 − 13 = 14. Structure (in words): a central nucleus containing 13 protons and 14 neutrons, with 13 electrons revolving around it in three shells — 2 electrons in the K shell, 8 in the L shell and 3 in the M shell (arrangement 2, 8, 3). Electronic configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1.

Q: ii. The energy of an electron in K and L shells is the same or different. Explain.

Ans: It is different. Each shell has a fixed energy, and the energy of a shell increases with its distance from the nucleus. The K shell (n = 1) is nearest to the nucleus, so its electrons have the least energy. The L shell (n = 2) is farther from the nucleus, so its electrons have higher energy than the electrons in the K shell. In general, the farther an electron is from the nucleus, the higher is its energy, and vice versa.

Q: iii. Draw the structures of hydrogen isotopes.

Ans: Hydrogen has three isotopes, and each has 1 proton and 1 electron; they differ only in the number of neutrons in the nucleus. Protium (1/1 H): nucleus contains 1 proton and no neutron, with 1 electron revolving in the K shell. Deuterium (2/1 H or D): nucleus contains 1 proton and 1 neutron, with 1 electron in the K shell. Tritium (3/1 H or T): nucleus contains 1 proton and 2 neutrons, with 1 electron in the K shell. So in a drawing, the circle for the orbit and the single electron stay the same in all three; only the neutrons inside the nucleus increase from 0 to 1 to 2.

Q: iv. How many electrons are present in each of the following atoms? Assuming that each is a neutral atom, identify the element. a. 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1 b. 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5 c. 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2

Ans: For a neutral atom: number of electrons = sum of the superscripts in the configuration, and this also equals the atomic number, which identifies the element.
a. Given: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1
Step 1: Add the superscripts: 2 + 2 + 6 + 1 = 11 electrons
Step 2: Atomic number = 11
Answer: 11 electrons — the element is Sodium (Na).
b. Given: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5
Step 1: Add the superscripts: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 5 = 17 electrons
Step 2: Atomic number = 17
Answer: 17 electrons — the element is Chlorine (Cl).
c. Given: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2
Step 1: Add the superscripts: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 20 electrons
Step 2: Atomic number = 20
Answer: 20 electrons — the element is Calcium (Ca).

Q: v. Why an atom is considered as neutral particle? Give reason(s).

Ans: An atom is neutral because the number of positively charged protons in its nucleus is exactly equal to the number of negatively charged electrons revolving around the nucleus. The charge on one proton (+1.6022 x 10^-19 C) is equal in size to the charge on one electron (−1.6022 x 10^-19 C), so the total positive charge and the total negative charge cancel each other. Neutrons carry no charge, so they do not affect the neutrality of the atom.

Q: vi. The mass of an atom is present in its nucleus. Can you explain it?

Ans: Yes. The mass of an atom is almost entirely the mass of its protons and neutrons, and both of these particles are present in the nucleus. A proton has a mass of 1.0072766 a.m.u. and a neutron 1.0086654 a.m.u., whereas an electron has a mass of only 0.000548597 a.m.u. — a proton is about 1837 times and a neutron about 1842 times heavier than an electron. The mass of the electrons is therefore negligible, so practically the whole mass of the atom is concentrated in its nucleus, which is why the nucleus is very dense.

Q: vii. What is the reason that physical properties of the isotopes are different but their chemical properties are the same?

Ans: Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but different mass numbers, because they have the same number of protons and electrons but a different number of neutrons. Chemical properties depend on the number of electrons, especially the valence electrons, which is the same in all isotopes, so their chemical properties are the same. Physical properties such as mass, density, melting point and boiling point depend on the mass of the atom, which is different for each isotope because of the different number of neutrons, so their physical properties differ.

Q: viii. Draw the structures of carbon isotopes. Then write down the number of proton, neutron and electron.

Ans: Carbon (atomic number 6) has three isotopes. In each structure the nucleus is drawn in the centre with the electrons in two shells, 2 in the K shell and 4 in the L shell (arrangement 2, 4); only the neutrons in the nucleus change. Carbon-12 (12/6 C): 6 protons, 6 neutrons, 6 electrons. Carbon-13 (13/6 C): 6 protons, 7 neutrons, 6 electrons. Carbon-14 (14/6 C): 6 protons, 8 neutrons, 6 electrons. In each case neutrons = mass number − atomic number, e.g. for Carbon-14: 14 − 6 = 8.

Q: ix. How many electrons could be contained in the K, L, M and N energy levels.

Ans: Formula: The maximum number of electrons in a shell = 2n2, where n is the number of the shell.
K shell: n = 1
Substitution: 2(1)2 = 2 x 1 = 2 electrons
L shell: n = 2
Substitution: 2(2)2 = 2 x 4 = 8 electrons
M shell: n = 3
Substitution: 2(3)2 = 2 x 9 = 18 electrons
N shell: n = 4
Substitution: 2(4)2 = 2 x 16 = 32 electrons
Answer: K = 2, L = 8, M = 18 and N = 32 electrons.

Q: x. Write detailed electronic configurations for 7/3 Li, 12/6 C and 24/12 Mg.

Ans: The atomic number gives the number of electrons in a neutral atom, and the electrons fill the lowest energy sub-shells first (1s, then 2s, then 2p, then 3s, and so on).
Lithium, 7/3 Li: electrons = 3
Configuration: 1s2 2s1
Carbon, 12/6 C: electrons = 6
Configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p2
Magnesium, 24/12 Mg: electrons = 12
Configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2
Answer: Li = 1s2 2s1; C = 1s2 2s2 2p2; Mg = 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2.

Q: xi. Write the symbol for an isotope: (a) Containing one proton and two neutrons (b) For which the atomic number is one and there is one neutron (c) For which the atomic number is one and the mass number is also one.

Ans: Formula: Mass number (A) = number of protons (Z) + number of neutrons (N). One proton means the element is hydrogen (H), Z = 1.
(a) Given: protons = 1, neutrons = 2
Substitution: A = 1 + 2 = 3
Symbol: 3/1 H (tritium)
(b) Given: atomic number Z = 1, neutrons = 1
Substitution: A = 1 + 1 = 2
Symbol: 2/1 H (deuterium)
(c) Given: atomic number Z = 1, mass number A = 1
Neutrons: N = A − Z = 1 − 1 = 0
Symbol: 1/1 H (protium)
Answer: (a) 3/1 H, (b) 2/1 H, (c) 1/1 H.

Test Yourself (p.52)

Q: 1. Sodium has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. Write the electronic configuration of the sodium atom.

Ans: A neutral sodium atom has as many electrons as protons, so it has 11 electrons (the 12 neutrons only fix its mass number, 11 + 12 = 23). The electrons fill the shells in order, 2 in the K shell, 8 in the L shell and the remaining 1 in the M shell, i.e. arrangement 2, 8, 1. Detailed electronic configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1.

Q: 2. Potassium has the electronic arrangement 2,8,8,1. a. What is its proton number? b. Draw its electronic structure.

Ans: (a) In a neutral atom the proton number (atomic number) is equal to the total number of electrons. Total electrons = 2 + 8 + 8 + 1 = 19, so the proton number of potassium is 19. (b) Electronic structure (in words): draw a central nucleus labelled with 19 protons, and four shells around it — the first (K) shell with 2 electrons, the second (L) shell with 8 electrons, the third (M) shell with 8 electrons and the fourth (N) shell with 1 electron.

Q: 3. Write the electronic configurations of N, P and Ar.

Ans: Nitrogen, N (Z = 7, 7 electrons): 1s2 2s2 2p3 — shell arrangement 2, 5. Phosphorus, P (Z = 15, 15 electrons): 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3 — shell arrangement 2, 8, 5. Argon, Ar (Z = 18, 18 electrons): 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 — shell arrangement 2, 8, 8.

Activity 2.1 (p.46)

Q: Activity 2.1: Make a model/diagram based on Bohr's atomic theory. Display this model in your classroom/laboratory

Ans: Make the model as follows: take a board or chart and fix a small ball or circle in the centre for the positively charged nucleus. Draw three concentric circles around it for the first three energy levels or shells and label them 1, 2, 3 and K, L, M, as in Bohr's atomic model figure in this unit. Place small beads or dots on the circles as electrons, keeping each electron on a fixed circle, because in Bohr's theory an electron revolves in a fixed orbit of fixed energy and cannot stay in between two orbits. Label the parts 'Nucleus' and 'Energy levels or shell'. Displayed in this way, the model shows that the K-shell (n = 1) is nearest to the nucleus and has the least energy, the L-shell (n = 2) is next and is higher in energy than the K-shell, and so on.

mcqs.q: Aluminium is represented as 27/13 Al. How many neutrons does it have and what is its electronic configuration?
mcqs.why: Formula: Neutrons = A - Z. Substitution: Neutrons = 27 - 13 = 14. The atom has 13 electrons arranged 2, 8, 3, giving the detailed configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1.

mcqs.q: Is the energy of an electron in the K shell the same as in the L shell?
options: Yes, all shells have exactly the same energy
No, K shell electrons have higher energy than L shell electrons
Energy depends only on the number of neutrons in the nucleus
No, it is different; L shell electrons have higher energy than K shell electrons
mcqs.why: Each shell has a fixed energy which increases with distance from the nucleus. The K shell, n = 1, is nearest and has the least energy, while the L shell, n = 2, is farther and its electrons have higher energy.

mcqs.q: The configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5 belongs to which neutral element?
mcqs.why: For a neutral atom, electrons = sum of the superscripts. Substitution: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 5 = 17 electrons. Atomic number 17 identifies the element as chlorine, Cl.

mcqs.q: Why is an atom considered a neutral particle?
options: Because it contains neutrons which carry a negative charge
Because electrons carry no charge at all
Because the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so their charges cancel each other
Because protons carry no charge at all
mcqs.why: One proton has charge +1.6022x10^-19 C and one electron has charge -1.6022x10^-19 C, equal in size and opposite in sign. Equal numbers of protons and electrons cancel, and neutrons carry no charge, so the atom is neutral.

mcqs.q: Why do isotopes have the same chemical properties but different physical properties?
options: Chemical properties depend on neutrons, while physical properties depend on protons
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, so their masses are the same
Chemical properties depend on electrons, which are the same, while physical properties depend on mass, which differs
Both chemical and physical properties depend only on the atomic number
mcqs.why: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, especially valence electrons, so their chemical properties are the same. Their neutron numbers and masses differ, so mass-dependent physical properties such as density and melting point differ.

mcqs.q: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are present in carbon-14, 14/6 C?
mcqs.why: Formula: Protons = Z = 6, and electrons = protons = 6 in a neutral atom. Formula: Neutrons = A - Z. Substitution: Neutrons = 14 - 6 = 8. So carbon-14 has 6 protons, 8 neutrons and 6 electrons.

mcqs.q: How many electrons can the M shell contain at maximum?
mcqs.why: Formula: Maximum electrons in a shell = 2n2. For the M shell n = 3. Substitution: 2(3)2 = 2 x 9 = 18 electrons. In the same way K holds 2, L holds 8 and N holds 32 electrons.

mcqs.q: Write the detailed electronic configuration of magnesium, 24/12 Mg.
mcqs.why: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so a neutral atom has 12 electrons. Electrons fill the lowest sub-shells first: 1s takes 2, 2s takes 2, 2p takes 6 and 3s takes the remaining 2, giving 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2.

mcqs.q: Potassium has the electronic arrangement 2,8,8,1. What is its proton number?
mcqs.why: In a neutral atom the proton number equals the total number of electrons. Substitution: Total electrons = 2 + 8 + 8 + 1 = 19. So the proton number, that is atomic number, of potassium is 19.

mcqs.q: In the model made for Activity 2.1 based on Bohr's atomic theory, how are the electrons placed?
options: Electrons are placed anywhere between the circles at random
All electrons are placed inside the nucleus with the protons
Each electron is placed on a fixed circle of fixed energy and cannot stay in between two orbits
Electrons are placed on one single circle regardless of energy
mcqs.why: In Bohr's model the centre is the positively charged nucleus and the concentric circles are the energy levels K, L, M. An electron revolves in a fixed orbit of fixed energy and cannot stay in between two orbits.

lessons.title: Detailed Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Dalton's theory was the first scientific theory of the atom; atoms combine in small whole number ratios.
  • Two Dalton points were later modified: the atom is divisible, and atoms of the same element can have different masses as isotopes.
  • In Rutherford's gold foil experiment most alpha particles passed straight through, showing most of the atom is empty.
  • Rutherford concluded that the atom has a small, positive, dense central nucleus with electrons revolving around it.
  • Bohr proposed fixed circular orbits of fixed energy in which an electron does not radiate energy.
  • An electron radiates energy when it falls to a lower orbit and absorbs energy when it jumps to a higher orbit.
  • Neutrons = A - Z, for example 131/54 Xe has 77 neutrons and 59/27 Co has 32 neutrons.
  • Sub-shells s, p, d, f hold a maximum of 2, 6, 10 and 14 electrons respectively.

Solved Exercises

Exercise — Long Questions

Q: (i) Why Dalton's atomic theory is considered as a base for modern atomic concepts?

Ans: Dalton's theory (1808) was the first scientific theory of the atom, and modern atomic concepts are built on it. Its main postulates were: matter is composed of very small particles called atoms; an atom is indivisible; atoms of a particular element are identical in size, shape, mass and other properties; atoms of different elements are different; atoms combine with each other in small whole-number ratios; and all chemical reactions are due to the combination or separation of atoms. Although later research modified two points — the atom is divisible into subatomic particles, and atoms of the same element can have different masses (isotopes) — the central ideas that matter is particulate, that atoms of different elements differ, that they combine in fixed whole-number ratios and that reactions are a rearrangement of atoms are still accepted. That is why Dalton's theory is regarded as the base of modern atomic concepts.

Q: (ii) Summarize Rutherford's model of an atom and explain how he developed this model based on the results of his famous gold-foil experiment.

Ans: The experiment (1911): Rutherford bombarded a very thin (0.0004 cm) gold foil with alpha (a-) particles from a radioactive source (polonium, 20,000 particles). The foil was surrounded by a photographic plate or zinc sulphide (ZnS) fluorescent screen to detect the particles coming out. Observations: most of the a-particles passed through the foil without any change in direction, which showed that most of the volume occupied by an atom is empty; some a-particles (8) were deflected by a smaller angle, and only a few (2) bounced back at their original way. Conclusions and the model: since a-particles are positively charged and similar charges repel each other, the particles that came back or were deflected must have passed near a positive portion in the centre of the atom. Rutherford concluded that: 1. An atom consists of a positively charged central portion called the nucleus, which contains protons and neutrons. 2. Electrons revolve around the nucleus with very high speed, just like the planets around the sun (the planetary model). 3. The attractive force of the nucleus on the electrons provides the centripetal force for their revolution. 4. The size of the nucleus is very small compared with the size of the atom, and most of the volume of the atom is empty. 5. The atom is neutral, as the number of electrons is numerically equal to that of protons. 6. The nucleus is responsible for the mass and energy of the atom.

Q: (iii) State the postulates which Bohr suggested to overcome the shortcomings of the Rutherford's atomic model.

Ans: Bohr (1913) took the hydrogen atom as a model and gave the following postulates: 1. Electrons are revolving around the nucleus in one of the fixed circular paths called shells or orbits. Each orbit has a fixed energy, so these orbits are also called energy levels. 2. The energy of the electron in an orbit is proportional to its distance from the nucleus; the farther the electron from the nucleus, the higher will be the energy, and vice versa. 3. As long as electrons are revolving around the nucleus in a fixed circular orbit, they do not gain or lose energy, i.e. the energy of an orbit is fixed. 4. When an electron jumps from a higher energy orbit to a lower energy orbit, it radiates energy, and when it jumps from a lower energy orbit to a higher energy orbit, it absorbs energy. The energy difference between two levels is given by dE = E2 − E1 = hu, where h is Planck's constant and u is frequency. 5. An electron can reside in any one of the orbits and cannot stay in between them. 6. The angular momentum (mvr) of an electron is an integral multiple of h/2pi, i.e. mvr = nh/2pi, where n is the number of the shell. In this way Bohr explained the stability of the atom and its line spectrum, which Rutherford's model could not explain.

Q: (iv) Complete the following table for neutral atoms of specific isotopes: (columns: Isotopic Symbol, Atomic No., Mass No., Number of Protons, Number of electrons, Number of neutrons) a. 131/54 Xe b. 59/27 Co c. 144/60 Nd d. 48/22 Ti e. 178/72 Hf f. 128/52 Te g. 40/18 Ar

Ans: Rules used: Number of protons = atomic number (Z). For a neutral atom, number of electrons = number of protons = Z. Formula: Number of neutrons = mass number (A) − atomic number (Z).
a. 131/54 Xe: Atomic No. = 54, Mass No. = 131, Protons = 54, Electrons = 54, Neutrons = 131 − 54 = 77
b. 59/27 Co: Atomic No. = 27, Mass No. = 59, Protons = 27, Electrons = 27, Neutrons = 59 − 27 = 32
c. 144/60 Nd: Atomic No. = 60, Mass No. = 144, Protons = 60, Electrons = 60, Neutrons = 144 − 60 = 84
d. 48/22 Ti: Atomic No. = 22, Mass No. = 48, Protons = 22, Electrons = 22, Neutrons = 48 − 22 = 26
e. 178/72 Hf: Atomic No. = 72, Mass No. = 178, Protons = 72, Electrons = 72, Neutrons = 178 − 72 = 106
f. 128/52 Te: Atomic No. = 52, Mass No. = 128, Protons = 52, Electrons = 52, Neutrons = 128 − 52 = 76
g. 40/18 Ar: Atomic No. = 18, Mass No. = 40, Protons = 18, Electrons = 18, Neutrons = 40 − 18 = 22
Answer: Neutrons are 77, 32, 84, 26, 106, 76 and 22 for rows a to g respectively, and in every row protons = electrons = atomic number.

Q: (v) (a) Define energy level and sub-energy level. (b) Explain the distribution of electrons in various energy levels and sub energy levels for first four elements of the periodic table.

Ans: (a) Energy level: According to Bohr's theory, electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed circular paths called shells or orbits, and each shell has a fixed energy; these shells are called energy levels. They are represented by K, L, M, N or by n = 1, 2, 3, 4... Sub-energy level (sub-shell): a shell or energy level is further divided into sub-shells or sub-energy levels. There are four sub-shells, represented by s, p, d and f (spectroscopic terms for sharp, principal, diffused and fundamental), which can hold a maximum of 2, 6, 10 and 14 electrons respectively. (b) Distribution for the first four elements: Hydrogen (Z = 1): 1 electron, in the K energy level, sub-shell 1s — configuration 1s1 (shell arrangement: K = 1). Helium (Z = 2): 2 electrons, both in the K level, sub-shell 1s — configuration 1s2 (K = 2; the K shell is now complete). Lithium (Z = 3): 2 electrons in the K level (1s2) and the third electron in the L level, sub-shell 2s — configuration 1s2 2s1 (K = 2, L = 1). Beryllium (Z = 4): 2 electrons in the K level (1s2) and 2 in the L level, sub-shell 2s — configuration 1s2 2s2 (K = 2, L = 2). Electrons thus fill the lowest energy level and sub-shell available first.

mcqs.q: According to Dalton's atomic theory, how do atoms combine with each other?
options: In any random ratio with no fixed proportion
Only in the ratio of their atomic masses
By dividing into smaller particles before combining
mcqs.why: Dalton proposed that atoms of different elements combine in small whole-number ratios and that chemical reactions are due to the combination or separation of atoms. This idea of fixed whole-number combining ratios is still accepted in modern concepts.

mcqs.q: Which two points of Dalton's theory were modified by later research?
options: Atoms of different elements are identical, and atoms never combine
Matter is not made of atoms, and reactions create new atoms
Atoms combine in whole-number ratios, and atoms of different elements differ
The atom is divisible into subatomic particles, and atoms of the same element can have different masses (isotopes)
mcqs.why: Later research showed the atom is divisible into protons, neutrons and electrons, and that atoms of the same element can have different masses as isotopes. The other Dalton ideas, such as atoms combining in whole-number ratios, are still accepted.

mcqs.q: In Rutherford's gold foil experiment, most alpha particles passed through the foil without any change in direction. What did this show?
options: Most of the volume occupied by an atom is empty
The atom is completely solid throughout
The nucleus fills most of the volume of the atom
mcqs.why: A very thin gold foil was bombarded with alpha particles and most passed straight through undeflected. This was only possible if most of the volume of the atom is empty space, with the mass concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford conclude about the centre of the atom from the particles that bounced back?
options: There is a negatively charged central portion called the nucleus
The centre of the atom is completely empty
There is a positively charged central portion called the nucleus
mcqs.why: Alpha particles are positively charged and like charges repel. The few particles that bounced back or were deflected must have passed near a positive portion in the centre, which Rutherford called the nucleus.

mcqs.q: According to Bohr's postulates, what happens while an electron revolves in a fixed circular orbit?
options: It continuously radiates energy and falls into the nucleus
It continuously absorbs energy from the nucleus
It does not gain or lose energy; the energy of the orbit is fixed
Its energy changes at every step of the orbit
mcqs.why: Bohr proposed that electrons revolve in fixed circular paths called shells or energy levels, each with fixed energy. As long as the electron stays in one such orbit it neither gains nor loses energy, which explained the stability of the atom.

mcqs.q: When does an electron radiate energy according to Bohr's theory?
options: When it jumps from a higher energy orbit to a lower energy orbit
When it jumps from a lower energy orbit to a higher energy orbit
While it stays in the same fixed orbit
When it stops revolving around the nucleus
mcqs.why: Bohr stated that an electron radiates energy when it falls from a higher to a lower energy orbit, and absorbs energy when it jumps from a lower to a higher orbit. The energy difference is given by dE = E2 - E1 = hu.

mcqs.q: How many neutrons are present in 131/54 Xe?
mcqs.why: Formula: Number of neutrons = mass number A - atomic number Z. Substitution: Neutrons = 131 - 54 = 77. Xenon-131 also has 54 protons and, as a neutral atom, 54 electrons.
